buttonLabel: "Explore the culture of Argentina, Chile and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  On a journey through Argentina, Chile and Uruguay, cultural stops are distributed
  unevenly. Buenos Aires offers tango, historic neighborhoods and gaucho traditions;
  Santiago introduces the history of Chile's capital; and Montevideo offers a
  different perspective on the cities of the Río de la Plata. We compare four
  available itineraries and the time allotted to each country.
---

## Three capitals, but different amounts of time to explore them

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring **Argentina, Chile and Uruguay** as main countries and a cultural and historical theme. The principal points of interest are [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). However, travelers spend different amounts of time in these cities: on some itineraries, Montevideo is only a day trip from Buenos Aires, while much of the journey is devoted to Patagonia, Iguazú, the Andes or other countries.

That is why the number of countries in the title is not enough. Compare the **actual cultural excursions**, how travelers cross from Argentina into Uruguay, and how much time remains after long transfers. Tours in this filter also visit Brazil, and some continue to Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. The three selected countries are a subset of the full geography, not a new continuous three-country itinerary.

The [general Argentina, Chile and Uruguay selection](/multi-country/argentina_chile_uruguay/) displays itineraries regardless of interest. Here we examine the cultural component; other country combinations are available under [multi-country culture and history tours](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Argentina: from Plaza de Mayo to tango and gauchos

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a sightseeing tour introduces Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada, [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/), San Telmo and Recoleta. In a few hours, you can see the political center, historic architecture and neighborhoods associated with the urban culture of the Río de la Plata. Buenos Aires is also rewarding for independent walks, provided they fit between excursions and flights.

The [17-day tour of four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) adds a **tango show with dinner** and a separate day at a ranch with a gaucho fiesta. The cultural theme extends beyond the capital's buildings: at the ranch, guests encounter the traditions of the Argentine Pampas. The specific arrangements and languages of group excursions should be compared with the private transfers on the same trip.

The [grand 26-day Argentina and Patagonia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) goes far beyond the capital. It travels through Salta, Purmamarca, Cafayate, Mendoza's wine regions and the lake district around Bariloche. Architecture, food and regional traditions enrich the Buenos Aires experience, but a large part of the 26 days is also devoted to mountain and nature routes. A longer trip does not automatically mean a more extensive museum program.

## Chile: historic Santiago before Patagonia or Atacama

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), itineraries visit La Moneda Palace, [Plaza de Armas](/chile/place/santiago-plaza-de-armas/) and old administrative buildings. Comparing these neighborhoods with Buenos Aires reveals how two cities with a shared Spanish colonial heritage developed on opposite sides of the Andes.

On the [17-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/), the journey starts in Santiago and continues to Punta Arenas, [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). The park, lakes and mountain panoramas form the nature-focused part of the tour. It would be a mistake to count every stop in Chile as a cultural excursion just because the entire itinerary carries a cultural theme.

The [20-day itinerary across six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day trip through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) travel from their Santiago sightseeing tours to Atacama and high-altitude Bolivia. If Chilean history is your priority, compare the actual hours in the capital rather than the total number of days on the continent. An Andean itinerary requires an entirely different pace and preparation.

## Uruguay: one full day in Montevideo

The Uruguayan part of this selection focuses mainly on [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Highlights include Independence Square, the historic center, the cathedral and old city buildings. Here travelers can compare the two shores of the Río de la Plata: Buenos Aires with its extensive districts and Uruguay's more compact capital.

The [four-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) includes a **full-day excursion to Montevideo from Buenos Aires**. On the [26-day trip](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), Uruguay also appears as a separate episode in a larger Argentine itinerary. The [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) contains a Montevideo excursion module, even though the city's name is not necessarily in a numbered day's heading. The [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) allocates day nine to Montevideo.

**A day in Montevideo is not the same as a full journey through Uruguay.** These programs do not automatically include Colonia del Sacramento or Punta del Este. To explore several Uruguayan cities, compare the itineraries in the [Argentina–Brazil–Uruguay cultural selection](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_uruguay/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Four available itineraries: what to compare

| Itinerary | Main cultural highlights |
|---|---|
| [4 countries, 17 days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) | Santiago, tango, a ranch and Montevideo |
| [6 countries, 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Three capitals and Andean monuments |
| [Argentina, 26 days](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) | Regional traditions and Patagonia |
| [8 countries, 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | Three capitals, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia |

The **17-day trip** combines urban history with Patagonia, Iguazú and Brazil. The **20-day itinerary** adds Bolivian and Peruvian landmarks. **32 days** allow for Ecuador and Colombia. On the **26-day itinerary**, Argentina's cultural stops are spread between the northwest, wine regions and the capital.

Duration alone tells you little here. It is more useful to compare sightseeing days in the three capitals, check what the tango evening and ranch visit include, and identify the cultural sites visited in the Andean countries when they feature in the complete itinerary.

## The Río de la Plata, borders and actual sightseeing time

For an itinerary involving a day trip by ferry to Montevideo, find out in advance how many hours remain **after travel and border formalities**. Depending on the tour and operator, confirm the departure port, ferry check-in time, baggage arrangements and return time. If transport takes up almost the entire day, there will be less opportunity to explore the historic center independently.

The countries have different national currencies: the Argentine, Chilean and Uruguayan pesos. Whether a particular bank card, tickets or cash can be used should be checked for each trip and card issuer; visa requirements depend on nationality and every country actually visited on the full route, including Brazil.

We help coordinate the sequence of excursions, flights and transfers. For a more focused choice, explore [cultural tours in Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/), [Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/) and [Uruguay](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/uruguay/).

## Frequently asked questions about the culture of Argentina, Chile and Uruguay

### Which tour includes both tango and gaucho traditions?

The [17-day trip through four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) includes a tango show and a day at a ranch with a gaucho fiesta. Both activities take place in Argentina.

### Is an overnight stay in Montevideo essential?

No. The featured itineraries include day trips to Uruguay's capital from Buenos Aires. This leaves less time for museums and walks than an overnight stay.

### Is Torres del Paine part of Chile's cultural heritage itinerary?

The national park is primarily a nature stop. The cultural portion of the Chilean leg takes place in Santiago. If museums and architecture matter most, assess the time allotted to the capital's sightseeing tour.

### Why does this selection include an eight-country tour?

The filter displays trips where all three selected countries form part of the main itinerary and culture is among the themes. The [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) does indeed visit five other countries. The filter's title does not reduce the trip's full geography.

## Argentina, Chile and Uruguay: where the wine experiences actually take place

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} traveling through Argentina, Chile and Uruguay as main countries. For someone choosing a trip for its wine and regional cuisine, the crucial question is **which tastings are included in the itinerary and which are offered at additional cost**.

[Argentina](/argentina/) features several winemaking regions on the 26-day itinerary: [Cafayate](/argentina/place/cafayate/), [Luján de Cuyo](/argentina/place/lujan-de-cuyo/) and the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/). Wine experiences occupy dedicated days, including winery visits and lunches overlooking the Andes.

In [Chile](/chile/), the experience depends on the itinerary. On the 20-day route, following a visit to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), travelers can separately book a tasting excursion to wineries in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/). The price and minimum group size are conditions of that optional excursion. On the 26-day route, the Chilean section visits Torres del Paine National Park and Milodón Cave. **A wine tasting in Chile is not confirmed for that tour.**

On both itineraries, [Uruguay](/uruguay/) is represented by [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), followed by a ferry back to Buenos Aires. The 26-day program includes a market visit and an introduction to local produce during the city tour. However, visits to Uruguayan wineries and tastings of local Tannat wines are not included in the confirmed programs.

## Which tours are best for exploring wine?

The [26-day Argentina and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) suits travelers looking for a substantial Argentinian wine experience. After Buenos Aires and Montevideo, guests visit Iguazú, northwestern Argentina and the Mendoza region before traveling on to Patagonia. Chile provides a mountain and nature segment rather than a wine excursion.

[Six Latin American countries in 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) is a shorter yet geographically extensive route through Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Buenos Aires has a tango show with dinner on the schedule. Santiago features a city tour, and a tasting excursion to Maipo can be added. The journey then continues toward Atacama and the Bolivian highlands.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_source_vsya_argentina}}

One tour offers more wine experiences in Argentina; the other lets you add a tasting in Chile. **Neither is an exclusively three-country wine tour:** both cover additional destinations. The number of countries in a filter is no substitute for the day-by-day itinerary and booking terms.

## Cafayate, Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley: three different wine experiences

[Cafayate](/argentina/place/cafayate/) comes after Salta on the itinerary. Travelers learn about grape growing and winemaking, visit a winery and a wine museum. The itinerary also includes an overnight stay at a wine hotel. This leg combines gastronomy with northwestern Argentina's scenery.

[Luján de Cuyo](/argentina/place/lujan-de-cuyo/) is visited later, in the [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) area. Three wineries are scheduled, with guided visits and tastings. The region is known for Malbec. Lunch is served at the third winery with views of the Andes. This is a group excursion with an English-speaking guide.

The following day is devoted to the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/): two more wineries, lunch and a return to Mendoza. Spreading these visits across two days makes it possible to see different estates without trying to squeeze the entire wine region into a brief stop. Specific brands, tasting flights and visit times are coordinated according to the confirmed schedule.

For other trips focused on the same interest, consult the [Argentina food and wine tour catalog](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/). It helps compare journeys with fewer countries if wineries matter more than long transfers.

## Maipo Valley: an optional wine excursion at extra cost

The [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) lies in the wine country around Santiago and is known, among other varieties, for Cabernet Sauvignon. On the 20-day itinerary, a winery excursion with tasting is listed **as an additional service costing $230 per person, with a minimum of 2 participants**. This is the price of the optional excursion, not the entire trip. The basic itinerary is not confirmed to include a Maipo winery visit.

Because a Santiago city tour is also scheduled, time for the Maipo excursion must be coordinated in advance. The next stage goes to San Pedro de Atacama and then Bolivia. Do not assume a full free day at wineries without checking the order of excursions and flights.

On the 26-day itinerary, Chile is visited far to the south, in Patagonia. Torres del Paine National Park and Maipo Valley lie in different parts of the country. Adding a Maipo tasting to a Patagonian day would require a separate restructuring of the itinerary. To explore other Chilean options, start with [food and wine tours in Chile](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/).

## Montevideo: discovering local food in one day

Travelers take a ferry from [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) to Montevideo and return the same day. On the 26-day itinerary, the sightseeing tour includes a city market where visitors can discover local ingredients and cuisine. On the 20-day itinerary, the principal stops are the port, Independence Square, the old town and the cathedral.

For food lovers, this is an interesting but time-limited stop. Sightseeing, a leisurely lunch, wine tasting and traveling out of Montevideo to a winery each require different amounts of time. All of these cannot be promised together when the actual itinerary calls for an evening return ferry.

If visiting wine estates is the main reason for traveling to Uruguay, that calls for individual planning. The region, travel arrangements, opening hours, tour language and need for an overnight stay must be established. Neither of the two tours examined includes such a segment.

## How to compare food and wine experiences rather than country counts

| Question | What is confirmed |
|---|---|
| Wineries in Argentina | The 26-day itinerary |
| Wine tasting in Chile | An optional excursion on the 20-day tour |
| Uruguayan local produce | Montevideo market on the 26-day tour |
| Total duration | 20 or 26 days |

When reviewing a trip, distinguish included tastings from an ordinary restaurant lunch and free time near a winery. For a wine-focused route, consider the number of estates, the guide, transport after tastings, exact visiting arrangements and whether dietary restrictions can be accommodated.

The Argentine winery days specify an English-speaking guide. Private Russian-language guiding must be arranged separately. After tastings, an organized transfer or a driver who does not drink alcohol is preferable.

If you intend to buy bottles of wine, check restrictions on liquids, checked baggage allowances and customs regulations in each successive country beforehand. Rules are not uniform across South America. Likewise, payment in Argentine, Chilean and Uruguayan pesos depends on the specific bank card and vendor.

The [general Argentina, Chile and Uruguay selection](/multi-country/argentina_chile_uruguay/) compares itineraries without a thematic filter, while [all multi-country food and wine journeys](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) offer other country combinations. Here, the focus is on the actual wine days included in specific available tours.

## Frequently asked questions about wine and gastronomy in Argentina, Chile and Uruguay

### Are Maipo Valley wineries included in the price of the 20-day tour?

No. The itinerary lists this as an optional excursion at $230 per person, with a minimum group of 2. The visit must be fitted around the Santiago sightseeing tour and subsequent flight.

### Which itinerary includes more winery visits?

The 26-day tour includes wineries in Cafayate, Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley. The 20-day tour includes dinner at a tango show, but the Chilean wine excursion is offered for an extra charge.

### Is there a wine tasting in Uruguay?

Neither current itinerary lists a winery visit. The 26-day trip includes an introduction to local products at the Montevideo market. A dedicated Uruguayan wine day would need separate arrangements.

### Is the 26-day tour suitable for someone interested only in wine?

It is a major journey with several substantial winery days in Argentina, as well as separate nature and cultural sections. Travelers primarily interested in wine should compare specialized tours or request a shorter private itinerary with newly calculated terms.

## Nature in Argentina, Chile and Uruguay: Patagonia or Atacama?

**To see the glaciers and mountains of Patagonia, choose itineraries with actual stops at Torres del Paine and El Calafate.** Not every route through Argentina, Chile and Uruguay visits them: some long South American journeys travel through Santiago and the northern Atacama Desert in Chile.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a nature theme, in which all three countries are part of the main itinerary. **Every matching tour also includes other countries**, especially Brazil, and some continue to Bolivia and Peru. This selected combination helps find overlapping countries, but the actual sequence is determined only by the itinerary.

Compare the full geography and travel arrangements under [Argentina + Chile + Uruguay](/multi-country/argentina_chile_uruguay/). Here the primary choice is about nature: Patagonian glaciers or northern Andean deserts, how long each takes and where Uruguay fits in.

## Chile: Torres del Paine and the very different Atacama

On the [17-day tour through four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/), the Chilean leg starts in Santiago, then continues via Puerto Natales to [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). According to the itinerary, travelers see rocky peaks, lakes, Salto Grande waterfall and Milodón Cave. The next section is in Argentina, around El Calafate.

The [26-day Argentina and Patagonia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) includes a full day at Torres del Paine within a longer journey through Argentina. It is another way to see the Chilean national park: the main itinerary follows Argentina's lake district and glacier regions.

But the [20-day route through six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [32-day tour through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) pass through Santiago and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile. They then continue to Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons. **Torres del Paine is not part of this Chilean section.** Atacama lies in northern Chile and is not a substitute for the Patagonian park: the landscapes, weather and logistics are entirely different.

## Argentina: Perito Moreno Glacier and Patagonia's lakes

For Patagonia itineraries, a key stop is [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) near [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). Viewing walkways offer views of the imposing ice face and the lake in front of it. On the 17-day route, the glacier excursion follows the transfer from Puerto Natales in Chile.

The 26-day tour devotes more days to Argentina's natural attractions. Its route includes [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) with lakes and forests, El Calafate, El Chaltén, Ushuaia and Tierra del Fuego National Park. Chile's Torres del Paine forms one stage of a long Patagonian journey. If the goal is to experience **several southern landscapes, rather than one glacier**, this route offers more nature stops, though it takes considerably longer.

An important distinction: views of the glacier on the Argentine side and the granite towers of the Chilean park do not show the same feature across a border. Despite their relative proximity, these are **two separate experiences**, so check that both have dedicated excursion days.

## Uruguay: the Río de la Plata shoreline, not a safari promise

On the current itineraries in this selection, Uruguay is chiefly a visit from [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). The city stands on the Río de la Plata, and its Rambla follows the waterfront. A coastal walk is a peaceful change of scene after long journeys, but sightseeing is usually limited to a day.

**Uruguay does not automatically add separate nature parks to these itineraries.** The actual programs do not substantiate several days on beaches, wilderness hikes or whale watching. Travelers who want more time by the ocean can separately explore [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) options in the [Argentina + Brazil + Uruguay nature selection](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_uruguay/interests/nature/).

This also affects the pace of each country. A Patagonian day may involve a long drive or a visit to viewpoints, whereas the Uruguayan stop can be a busy but short city excursion. Equal amounts of time should not be assigned to the three countries solely because they are all listed in a catalog.

## Choosing an itinerary by its nature days

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_tur_v_4_strany_yuzhnoj_ameriki,tour_source_vsya_argentina,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If your priority is **Patagonia**, compare the 17- and 26-day tours. The first combines Chile's Torres del Paine and Argentina's Perito Moreno in a more compact sequence; the second spends considerably more time in Argentina, including additional lake and mountain regions.

If you are more interested in **Atacama landscapes and Bolivia's highlands**, the 20- and 32-day itineraries offer a different nature experience. Uruguay is included, but most nature days are outside the Uruguayan leg. [Multi-country nature trips with Bolivia and Peru](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_peru/interests/nature/) provide a way to compare the northern Andean itinerary separately.

Do not confuse scenic landscapes with guaranteed animal sightings. Torres del Paine is home to wild birds and mammals, but a typical park excursion does not promise sightings of a particular species. For that objective, explore the separate [Wildlife and Safaris theme](/interests/wildlife/).

## Weather, trail access and long transfers

Weather can change quickly in Torres del Paine; wind and temperature call for warm layers and rain protection even during the warmer season. Official park rules restrict travel off designated paths and may change access to particular trails. **A sightseeing excursion and a multi-day trek are different products.** A hike is not included unless the itinerary explicitly states it.

At Perito Moreno, itineraries usually focus on organized viewing from established platforms. El Chaltén and the lake regions require different preparation if longer independent walks are chosen. For Atacama and Bolivia, the primary considerations are dry air, sunshine, altitude and a gradual approach to acclimatization. The same packing list and pace will not suit both destinations.

On the 17-day journey, Chile and Argentina are linked by an overland transfer between Puerto Natales and El Calafate. In the 26-day journey, the Chilean park is integrated into an Argentine itinerary. Uruguay requires a separate crossing or other transport from the Buenos Aires area, as specified by the tour. To protect the planned nature days, check connections and the documents needed to cross and recross borders according to each traveler's nationality.

Ada Tours helps coordinate the sequence of stops and transfers. The transport, guides and excursions included depend on the particular tour; optional activities and weather contingency days are not automatically part of every itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Chile and Uruguay

### Does every tour include Torres del Paine?

No. On the 20- and 32-day journeys, the Chilean leg passes through Atacama toward Bolivia. Torres del Paine is included in the 17- and 26-day Patagonia itineraries.

### Can I visit Perito Moreno and Torres del Paine on one trip?

Yes. The [17-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) and [26-day tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) include both attractions. Their sequence, overall pace and time devoted to other regions differ.

### Where can I see animals on this country combination?

The country names alone do not answer that. Uruguay is predominantly an urban stop here, while Chile and Argentina offer landscapes and nature excursions; sightings of specific animals are not guaranteed. Look for dedicated experiences in the [wildlife tour catalog](/interests/wildlife/tours/).

## Where to watch wildlife on a route through Argentina, Chile and Uruguay

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} through **Argentina, Chile and Uruguay** under the Wildlife and Safaris theme. At present, the matching itinerary is the [32-day eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/): its main wildlife experiences are on Ecuador's Galápagos Islands and near Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons. The trip also passes through Brazil, Peru and Colombia. Selecting three countries does not mean the journey runs only through them. The 17-, 20- and 26-day journeys mentioned below are scenery-focused alternatives under the Nature theme; they are not included in the current wildlife selection.

The nature-focused alternatives feature **Patagonia and Iguazú Falls** prominently. In [Argentina](/argentina/), individual programs include [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/), Bariloche's lake district and Tierra del Fuego. In [Chile](/chile/), there are [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), lakes and mountain valleys, or the dry Atacama Desert on itineraries continuing to Bolivia.

**The Uruguayan stop on all the itineraries discussed is primarily urban:** a trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) from Buenos Aires. These programs do not confirm marine wildlife watching, a nature reserve visit or a dedicated safari in Uruguay. Wildlife encounters on the 32-day trip are concentrated in other countries; the scenic alternatives belong to the separate Nature theme.

For a geographical selection without a theme filter, browse [all tours through Argentina, Chile and Uruguay](/multi-country/argentina_chile_uruguay/). Other routes featuring animal encounters are grouped under [Wildlife and Safaris](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/), while journeys focusing on glaciers, mountains and waterfalls appear under [Nature](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Nature alternatives in Chile: Torres del Paine and Atacama

On the [17-day four-country trip](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/), Chile's nature days start after exploring Santiago. The itinerary travels via Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine National Park. The excursion focuses on mountain peaks, valleys, lakes, waterfalls and the windswept open spaces of Patagonia. It is a good option for seeing high mountains and glacial scenery without undertaking a separate long expedition into Bolivia's highlands.

On the [26-day Argentina and Patagonia trip](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), Torres del Paine is one stage of an extensive Patagonian section that continues through Argentine glaciers, mountains and Tierra del Fuego. **More days do not necessarily mean more time inside the Chilean park itself:** much of the 26-day trip is allocated to Argentina's cities and nature regions.

The [20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [32-day journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) present a completely different side of Chile. After Santiago, both head to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and the Bolivian border. Nature here is chiefly represented by desert, dry mountain plains and high-altitude landscapes. Planned flamingo watching or dedicated bird excursions should not be attributed to Atacama unless they are specified in the selected day's itinerary. An interest in nature alone does not establish that a wildlife excursion is included.

## Nature alternatives in Argentina: glaciers, Bariloche and Tierra del Fuego

[El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) is the gateway to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in Los Glaciares National Park. The 17-day tour gives this attraction a dedicated day. Walkways to viewpoints let visitors observe the wall of ice and the lake scenery from different angles. The time spent at the glacier and the journey from El Calafate matter more than a simple mileage figure on a map.

On the 26-day itinerary, Argentina's nature geography is much more extensive: [Lake Nahuel Huapi](/argentina/place/nahuel-huapi-lake/), Bariloche, El Calafate, El Chaltén and [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) with Tierra del Fuego National Park. The variety of forests, lakes, mountains and glaciers allows travelers to experience several Patagonian regions in one journey. Nevertheless, a day by a lake does not automatically become an excursion to observe specific animal species.

On the 17-day four-country tour, the journey continues from the Patagonian parks to the Argentine side of Iguazú. This nature stop may also be part of the full itinerary on other journeys. [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and Brazil's [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) provide views of the waterfalls from different banks and walking trails. Brazil is an additional country on the actual itinerary even though it is absent from this selection's title.

## Uruguay: a day in Montevideo, not a nature safari

On the [17-day tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) and [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) has a dedicated excursion day. The 20-day journey also has a separate city excursion module, while the 26-day trip features an outing across the Río de la Plata.

The city program introduces the capital, its squares, historic center and waterfront. Ocean and river scenery provide a pleasant change of setting, but **a cultural city tour is not birdwatching, a reserve visit or marine mammal watching**. If Uruguay's wildlife is the primary goal, these four journeys do not contain a confirmed dedicated nature excursion in the country.

The Uruguayan day does offer a pause between an intensive nature itinerary and flights. Adding a distant nature area without checking the duration of ferry crossings and transfers would be inappropriate.

## Wildlife, seasons and preparation: what to check before choosing a tour

Nature areas can be home to many bird and mammal species, but **a park appearing on an itinerary does not guarantee an encounter with a specific animal**. If you want to see birds, penguins or marine wildlife, the itinerary needs a separate confirmed activity with an appropriate season and enough time. Neither a general Iguazú visit nor viewing a glacier automatically qualifies as a safari.

Clothing needs to cover several natural zones. At the waterfalls, splash protection and non-slip shoes are useful; on Patagonian excursions, prepare for wind, rain and cold. Traveling across Chile's Atacama toward Bolivia's lagoons brings altitude, dry air and sharp differences between daytime and nighttime temperatures. Even when traveling by vehicle, altitude and exertion must be considered separately.

Especially on a shorter trip, find out **how much time is actually left for walks** and how much will be spent on flights, ferries and border transfers. Multi-country journeys require checking all participants' travel documents and baggage limits for the actual flights. We help coordinate nature stops, transfers and the pace of the itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Chile and Uruguay

### Can travelers see whales in Uruguay on these itineraries?

**A dedicated whale-watching excursion is not confirmed on any of the four itineraries discussed.** Montevideo is primarily an urban stop. Marine wildlife watching would require a separate tour with an appropriate season and location.

### Is Argentina or Chile better for glaciers?

On the [17-day tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/), the principal dedicated glacier day is at Argentina's Perito Moreno, while the Chilean section mainly features Torres del Paine. The 26-day itinerary covers a wider range of Argentina's natural regions. Compare the actual days rather than the general fame of the region.

### Why does a Wildlife and Safaris selection include a trip to Montevideo?

Because the wildlife encounters belong to the **full 32-day trip**: its principal wildlife sections are the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador and Bolivia's lagoons. Uruguay is part of the main geography, but its excursion is cultural. The 17-, 20- and 26-day scenic programs are mentioned for comparison and belong to the Nature selection.

### Do all four journeys include the Galápagos?

No. The [Galápagos Islands](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) appear on the 32-day journey through Ecuador. The other itineraries differ in duration and nature stops; they do not imply the same set of animals and parks.

## Argentina and Colombia on one tour: how the route works

**For a journey through Argentina and Colombia, we offer an extended trip across eight countries.** It is the [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days: From Rio and Iguazú to the Galápagos and Colombia”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), running from October 22 to November 22, 2026.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Argentina and Colombia are both part of the main itinerary, but **they are not visited one immediately after the other**. The tour begins in Brazil, then includes the Argentine side of Iguazú, Buenos Aires and an excursion to Montevideo. From Argentina, travelers fly to Chile, cross Bolivia and Peru, visit Ecuador and only then arrive in Colombia.

This distinction matters when choosing a trip. If you want a short journey specifically from **Buenos Aires to Bogotá**, the featured itinerary is not a ready-made two-country product. Its purpose is to explore different parts of South America on one connected, guided expedition.

| Stage | Itinerary days |
|---|---|
| Argentina | 7–10 |
| Intermediate countries | 10–25 |
| Colombia | 26–32 |

These numbers refer to the sequence of the one published tour. Day 10 begins in Argentina and ends with arrival in Chile, so the stages partly overlap on that day.

## Argentina: both sides of Iguazú, Buenos Aires and tango

The itinerary first visits the waterfalls from the Brazilian side, then **crosses to the Argentine side of Iguazú on day 7**. [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) is the gateway to the national park's trails. Viewing the falls from both banks provides different perspectives on the same river system, and the two parks have separate admission and border-entry requirements. After the excursion, travelers transfer to the airport and fly to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

Day 8 includes a group sightseeing tour of the capital lasting about three hours, with a Russian-speaking guide. A tango show with dinner follows in the evening. Unlike the nature-focused waterfall day, this part explores urban neighborhoods and a living cultural tradition. If specific city architecture interests you, explore [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/) and [Recoleta](/argentina/place/recoleta/): these districts reveal just how varied Buenos Aires can be.

Day 9 is a trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Under the current itinerary, guests leave early for the port, cross the Río de la Plata by ferry, spend a sightseeing day in Uruguay with an English-speaking guide and return to Buenos Aires. Ferry tickets are listed as included. It is **a separate visit to another country** with its own immigration requirements, even though the group returns to the same hotel that evening.

Day 10 involves an airport transfer and a flight to Santiago de Chile. **There is no direct transfer from Argentina to Colombia on this itinerary.** The Colombian leg begins only after several other countries have been visited.

## What happens between Argentina and Colombia?

After [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), travelers explore Chile. The plan includes Santiago, a flight to Calama and accommodation in [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). A nighttime astronomy excursion here is optional, not a guaranteed activity on every departure.

The journey then continues across Bolivia's highlands for two days in 4×4 vehicles, passing lagoons, desert landscapes, geothermal areas and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). According to the itinerary, some sections are **above 4,000 m**, with an overnight stay in an expedition-style hotel. The next leg travels to La Paz, then via Tiwanaku and the Peruvian border to Lake Titicaca.

Peru includes a visit to Cusco, [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and a guided tour of Lima. Day 21 features a flight to Quito, followed by the Ecuadorian section with the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) and Guayaquil.

The route is logistically demanding. It combines international flights, a ferry to Uruguay, overland crossings of Andean borders, off-road high-altitude sections and flights to islands. The overall duration of 32 days matters, but so does the number of days on which travel and excursions are scheduled together.

### Can the journey be shortened to just two countries?

The published itinerary **does not offer this as a separate ready-made option**. Going directly from Argentina to Colombia would involve a different set of flights, overnight stays, excursions and services. If you need only those two destinations, consult the [Argentina tour catalog](/argentina/tour/) and [Colombia tour catalog](/colombia/tour/), and consider a private combination under separately arranged terms. The 32-day program's price and included services cannot automatically be applied to a shorter version.

## Colombia: from Medellín to Bogotá

The Colombian part begins **on day 26**. After departing from Guayaquil in Ecuador, the group arrives in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), a major Andean city with the mild climate of the Aburrá Valley. Day 27 includes an excursion to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/).

Day 28 includes an introduction to Medellín and Comuna 13, followed by a flight to the Caribbean coast. In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), the group explores the historic city, including its fortifications, squares and buildings from different eras. The climate is noticeably different from the high-altitude sections, so light clothing replaces the heavier jacket needed in the Andes.

On day 30, travelers fly to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) for its historic center, museums and panoramic views from [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/). The final full sightseeing day is spent in [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) visiting the Salt Cathedral. Day 32 lists a flight from Bogotá to São Paulo, connecting with the flight home.

**Bogotá stands at an elevation of approximately 2,600 m.** After warm Cartagena and a succession of climate zones, travelers return to a cool high-altitude city. Colombia takes up the final seven days of this itinerary; reducing it to one or two cities would change the experience and require different transfer arrangements.

## Dates, climate and packing: October versus November

The published itinerary starts on October 22, 2026, and ends on November 22. The Argentine stops fall in late October, spring in the Southern Hemisphere. According to Argentina's tourism portal, spring is pleasant for walking around Buenos Aires, while Iguazú remains humid and subtropical. Bring a waterproof outer layer, suitable walking shoes and protection for electronics against spray at the falls.

The Colombian stops take place in the second half of November. The Caribbean coast is hot and humid, while high-altitude Bogotá is much cooler. Between these countries, the route crosses highland deserts, Bolivia and Peru, where morning and nighttime temperatures can differ greatly from those by the sea. **Pack for both the coldest and warmest parts of the journey**, not just Argentina and Colombia.

On a long trip, several compatible layers, sturdy shoes, a small daypack and separately packed belongings for transfers are useful. Before flights, confirm baggage allowances for every segment. Transport being part of an organized tour does not guarantee identical weight limits on every flight.

## Documents, money and insurance for an eight-country itinerary

Although the selection is titled after two countries, **travel documentation must cover all eight**. The actual route includes Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. Entry rules, potential visas and transit requirements, passport validity, ticketing and overland border formalities must be checked for each nationality. Additional rules apply to the Galápagos: TCT registration, a conservation fee and biosecurity requirements.

Several currencies are used. Argentina uses the Argentine peso, Colombia the Colombian peso, and the Ecuadorian section the US dollar. Paying every small expense in a single currency will be impractical. Before departure, determine where local charges apply, which expenses are included in the tour and which are personal, and whether your cards work in every country. It is best not to quote currency exchange rates in the article because they change.

Insurance should cover **the full geography**, connections and high-altitude segments, not just the two countries in the title. Visiting Bolivia's highlands requires advance consideration of altitude tolerance and insurance coverage. Medical and immigration requirements should be checked against current official rules before departure.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I visit Argentina and Colombia on a single Ada Tours trip?

Yes. The [32-day eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes both Argentina and Colombia. It is a multi-country itinerary with other stages between the two countries, rather than a direct transfer.

### In what order are Argentina and Colombia visited?

First come the Argentine side of Iguazú Falls and Buenos Aires, followed by Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. The final seven days are devoted to Colombia: Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá.

### Is a tango evening included in Argentina?

Yes. Day 8 in Buenos Aires includes a tango show with dinner. Day 9 is a separate ferry excursion to Montevideo, followed by a return to Argentina.

### Why does the journey last 32 days?

The route covers eight countries, flights between cities, Uyuni and other high-altitude regions, Peru with Machu Picchu, the Galápagos Islands and Colombia's cities. Shortening it without changing the services and logistics would not constitute the same itinerary.

### Is there a direct flight from Argentina to Colombia within this tour?

No. On day 10 the itinerary flies from Buenos Aires to Santiago de Chile, while the group reaches Colombia from Guayaquil on day 26. These are two different stages of the longer trip.

### Which climatic conditions are hardest to combine?

Iguazú is warm and humid; Buenos Aires is in spring in late October; Bolivia's highlands can be cold; Cartagena is hot and Bogotá is at high altitude. Even when traveling in autumn, luggage needs to suit several temperature zones.

If you are choosing a shorter [tour of Argentina](/argentina/tour/) or [tour of Colombia](/colombia/tour/), compare the actual routes in those catalogs. For an extended journey across eight countries, use the complete [tour description](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/): it defines the included transfers, excursions and conditions.
